definition: Claude is a series of large language models (LLMs) developed by American software company Anthropic.
details: Claude was released as an AI-based chatbot in March 2023. It is also used in AI-assisted software development. Anthropic sells Claude-based agentic tools including Claude Code, a terminal coding agent, and Claude Cowork, a similar tool for non-programmers. Claude is trained using a constitution, a technique developed by Anthropic to improve ethical and legal compliance. Since Claude 3, each generation has typically been released in three sizes, named Haiku (the least capable), Sonnet, and Opus (the most capable). In 2026, an additional model named Claude Mythos was released to a handful of companies and organizations; this was followed by the release of Claude Fable, a version of Mythos with stricter safeguards, to the general public. In February 2026, the United States Department of Defense designated Anthropic a "supply chain risk" and federal agencies were ordered to phase out Claude after the company refused to remove contractual prohibitions on using Claude for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. A federal judge blocked the designation in March 2026 and permanently set it aside in August 2026 as unconstitutional retaliation.

explainer.lead: Claude is Anthropic's family of large language models, available as a chatbot and as the basis for tools that carry out tasks such as writing software. Its design and use raise practical questions about capability, safeguards, and who may control how an AI system is deployed.

tiers.eli5: Claude is a computer program that reads and writes language, a bit like a very well-read helper you can talk to. Anthropic taught it using a rulebook called a constitution to encourage behavior that follows ethical and legal rules. Different versions come in different sizes, much like choosing a small, medium, or large engine.
tiers.practitioner: Claude can be used for conversational tasks and AI-assisted software development. Claude Code operates as a terminal coding agent, while Claude Cowork offers similar agentic assistance for non-programmers. Since Claude 3, choosing among Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus has typically meant choosing between lower and higher capability, and safeguard restrictions can affect whether a requested task is permitted.
tiers.paperLevel: Claude denotes a series of large language models developed by Anthropic and trained using a constitution, Anthropic's technique for improving ethical and legal compliance. Since Claude 3, generations have typically comprised Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus variants in increasing order of capability. The source description does not provide an architecture, parameter counts, training corpus, evaluation results, or a formal training objective.

explainer.example: A programmer could ask Claude Code in a terminal to help with a software change. Claude Code would use a Claude model to assist with the coding task, rather than requiring the programmer to use only the chatbot interface.

flow: A user gives a request to the Claude chatbot or a Claude-based tool.
The selected Claude model processes the request using capabilities learned during training.
Constitutional training guides the model toward ethical and legal compliance.
Claude produces a language response or assists with a task through Claude Code or Claude Cowork.

explainer.whyItMatters: Claude combines general language assistance with agentic software tools and an explicit approach to ethical and legal compliance. Its contractual limits on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons also became central to a dispute with the United States Department of Defense in 2026; a federal judge blocked the resulting supply-chain-risk designation in March and permanently set it aside in August as unconstitutional retaliation.
